newsitem.title: JAPAN: Longer-end of U.S. Treasuries higher in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Longer-end of U.S. Treasuries higher in Tokyo.

text.p: The longer-end of U.S. Treasuries rose in Tokyo on Friday supported by healthy bids by local investors, traders said.

"The 10-year sector of Treasuries and corporate debt offering a yield of around seven percent is most popular among investors. Some traders bought the long bond afresh this morning," said a U.S. brokerage trader.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond was last traded at 95-22/32 to yield 6.97 percent, up from New York's 95-19/32.
The 6-5/8 percent 10-year note was last traded at 99-8/32 to yield 6.73 percent, up from New York's 99-5/32.
U.S. hedge funds along with central bank investors were said to have bought Treasuries overnight in New York, adding to the bullish sentiment in Tokyo.
Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) on Thursday launched a $500 million 7.125 percent straight bond due on June 13, 2007 at 99.815.
Traders said the issue was attracting good investor interest. The price had climbed to near par and the yield had fallen to around seven percent by Friday.
